scope: The re-run after review 5723093389: two learning pages on sjawhar/legion#2580, no code change, no changelog fragment, a reply to that review and a fresh approval at the new head. Generation 1's code, AGENTS.md sentence and settings descriptions are accepted and untouched.

implement: legion-worker: the phase's mechanics, with references/pr-body.md (the proof shape, and the body corrected before the push), references/skip-checks-trailer.md (the docs push carries no trailer; only a handoff-only push does), references/review-threads.md (the reply to review 5723093389) and references/default-branch-check.md.
asd-ste100: every edit is a sentence an agent reads without a human to resolve ambiguity, and the whole round exists because three such sentences pointed at the wrong code.
envoy: the completion report and any decision go to the architect's role topic.
test: legion-worker: the tester's phase, and references/pr-body.md for the proof entries; the plan's acceptance table is the finite list of commands to re-run at the head, the two tree comparisons and the required-check reads included.
envoy: reporting to the architect and asking the implementer through its role topic.
review: legion-worker: with references/review-threads.md (answering and resolving review 5723093389's threads) and references/merge-gate.md (the round must end in a GitHub approval at the new head, which this issue's acceptance names, since this repository's main ruleset does not dismiss a stale review on push).
asd-ste100: the three rewritten citations and the sentences around them are the whole change, so the review reads them as text that must be checkable without help.

findings.finding: The acceptance's 'neither page cites a line number' reaches five citations the architect's three items do not name (.github/workflows/ci.yaml:1544-1547 and :477-478, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2607, scripts/semantic-line-breaks.guides.test.ts:12 and :25-40), every one of which review 5723093389 certified as true at the head.
findings.answer: Decision D1: the acceptance is read literally for the two named pages, so all five go, each replaced by the anchor named in the plan's Task 1 table. The other two pr2580 pages keep their twelve line citations, since the spec and the architect's comment name two pages; the planner reported the inconsistency to the architect and offered the wider edit.

findings.finding: 'Say the guides test file holds three tests' fixes one sentence but leaves two more false clauses on the same page: the 'in one … in the other' enumeration, and 'the merge brought a second test' (it brought two; the file holds 1 test at c10800814dec and 3 from 1a9095e6cf22 on).
findings.answer: Task 1's table changes all three, separating the five files from the three tests and naming each test by its title.

findings.finding: The old parser sat in documentedClaims, not in the test function, and documentedClaims still exists at the head with the opposite behaviour, so a bare symbol citation sends the reader to code that contradicts the page.
findings.answer: Decision D3: the citation carries the symbol, the quoted old comment and the commit c10800814dec, and the page says what the head's claimListNames does instead.

findings.finding: 'Cite by symbol, not line number, as AGENTS.md asks' has no source: no AGENTS.md in the tree carries that rule; the rule that exists is skills/dispatch-writing-specs/SKILL.md, scoped to specs.
findings.answer: Decision D2: the requirement is this issue's acceptance, and the pull-request reply says so rather than citing a rule that is not in the tree. A project-wide rule for learning pages would be an edit of skills/legion-retro/references/learnings.md and is not this issue's.

findings.finding: The other two pr2580 pages carry twelve line-number citations that the same wording would catch; editing them would not void the approval, since only docs/solutions/ and .legion/<issue>/ may sit above it.
findings.answer: Decision D1 keeps them out of scope and names the choice for the architect.

findings.finding: 'Every citation matches the code at the new head' has no machine check, because nothing enumerates the citations; the reviewer did it by hand over about thirty.
findings.answer: The plan's acceptance table lists each citation the two pages will carry with its own grep, so the tester has a finite list: grep -Fn for a head citation, and for the historical one a pair (present at c10800814dec, absent at the head).

findings.finding: The 'no file outside docs/solutions/ and .legion/INFRA-841/' clause needs its base and its allowance spelled out: .legion/INFRA-841/ is already absent at f11e42a8, which retro removed.
findings.answer: The table gives the command verbatim (git diff --name-only 7e630849 <head> filtered) and says the clause allows those deletions and does not ask the directory to exist.

findings.finding: A reply to review 5723093389 does not unblock the merge: CHANGES_REQUESTED stands until a new review is submitted, and this repository's main ruleset sets dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push: false.
findings.answer: The plan makes a GitHub approval at the new head the review phase's own acceptance line, with gh pr view's reviewDecision and mergeStateStatus as the machine proxy; the reply is a comment and clears nothing by itself.

findings.finding: A push carrying skip-checks: true would leave ci-ok, a required context, unreported at the final head.
findings.answer: Decision D4: the docs push and retro's push carry no trailer; only handoff-only pushes do, and the table reads ci-ok and pr-title green at the final head.

findings.finding: 'Push once' contradicts the phase model: implement, test and review each write and push a handoff, and retro must remove .legion/INFRA-841/ again before READY.
findings.answer: Decision D4: 'once' is one push carrying the docs change; the handoff pushes and retro's removal are unchanged.

findings.finding: The pull-request body repeats the facts being corrected (the guides-test run, unscoped) and is published text the retro step keeps true.
findings.answer: Decision D5: the implementer corrects the body's guides-test sentence before the push, keeping the measured '1 pass, 0 fail' scoped to the first merge head, and changes nothing else.

findings.finding: Whether a changelog fragment is owed was left open.
findings.answer: Decision D5: none. docs/solutions/ is in no CHANGELOG_PACKAGES, and a fragment would be a file outside docs/solutions/, which the acceptance forbids.

findings.finding: Two acceptance clauses no machine can decide (the fresh approval, and 'every citation matches'), and the reply itself is read by a required check (check-pr-text.sh, re-run by pr-title.yaml on pull_request_review).
findings.answer: The plan names the machine proxies for both clauses and has the implementer read pr-title green after the reply as well as after the push, with no private name in the reply.

specDepartures.spec: Spec v3 names three citations to fix (MAX_LINE, wrapLongLine, the old parser) and the test count, while its acceptance says neither page cites a line number.
specDepartures.plan: The plan removes every line-number citation from the two named pages, five more than the three the review named, and replaces each with a symbol or a quoted phrase; it leaves the twelve line citations on the other two pr2580 pages alone.
specDepartures.evidence: The five are .github/workflows/ci.yaml:1544-1547 and :477-478, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2607, and scripts/semantic-line-breaks.guides.test.ts:12 and :25-40; all are true at the head today, and review 5723093389 says 'every other citation in all four pages is true at the head'. The last of them straddles two tests and delimits neither. Each has an anchor at the head: the workflow step named 'Test the semantic line-break checker', the test: path filter's two entries, the AGENTS.md sentence quoted by its opening clause, const GUIDES, and the three test titles.
